_note: Bibliographic records for the scholars and compilers this app's own corpus cites. Names, dates, schools and works are checkable bibliography. `biography` is null everywhere and stays null until verified text is supplied — the pages are not empty in the meantime, because each one shows the verses and topics derived from every layer that cites that scholar. Where `methodology` is filled in it is a one-line description of the work's own stated approach, and `description_source` says exactly that so it is never mistaken for a sourced claim. The last four entries exist because the corpus cites them, not because a list of great scholars was wanted.

scholars.title: Ibn Kathir
scholars.methodology: A tafsir of narration: the ayah is explained first by other ayat, then by hadith and the reports of the early generations, with weak reports named as weak.
scholars.description_source: Descriptive summary of the work's own stated approach — pending review against a cited introduction.

scholars.title: Al-Tabari
scholars.methodology: Collects the reported interpretations of an ayah with their chains of transmission, then states which reading he holds and why.
scholars.description_source: Descriptive summary of the work's own stated approach — pending review against a cited introduction.

scholars.title: Al-Qurtubi
scholars.methodology: Reads each ayah for the rulings it carries, surveying the positions of the schools alongside language and reported interpretation.
scholars.description_source: Descriptive summary of the work's own stated approach — pending review against a cited introduction.

scholars.title: Ibn Ashur
scholars.methodology: Attends closely to the language and rhetoric of the ayah, and to the purposes the ruling serves.
scholars.description_source: Descriptive summary of the work's own stated approach — pending review against a cited introduction.
